title: The Jew mocks the dove at the baptism
source_text: Ἵνα δὲ μὴ δοκῶμεν ἑκόντες διὰ τὸ ἀπορεῖν ἀπαντήσεως ὑπερβαίνειν αὐτοῦ τὰ κεφάλαια, ἐκρίναμεν ἕκαστον κατὰ δύναμιν λῦσαι τῶν ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ προτιθεμένων. φροντίσαντες οὐ τοῦ ἐν τῇ φύσει τῶν πραγμάτων εἱρμοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθίας ἀλλὰ τῆς τάξεως τῶν ἐν τῇ βίβλῳ αὐτοῦ ἀναγεγραμμένων. φέρ᾿ οὖν ἴδωμεν, τί ποτε καὶ λέγει διαβάλλων τὸ οἷον σωματικῶς ἑωραμένον ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος πνεῦμα ἅγιον εἴδει περιστερᾶς· ἔστι δ᾿ ὁ Ἰουδαῖος αὐτῷ ἔτι ταῦτα λέγων, πρὸς ὃν ὁμολογοῦμεν εἶναι κύριον ἡμῶν τὸν Ἰησοῦν· λουομένῳ, φησὶ, σοὶ παρὰ τῷ Ἰωάννῃ φάσμα ὄρνιθος ἐξ ἀέρος λέγεις ἐπιπτῆναι. εἶτα πυνθανόμενος ὁ παρ᾿ αὐτῷ Ἰουδαῖός φησι· τίς τοῦτο εἶδεν ἀξιόχρεως μάρτυς τὸ φάσμα, ἢ τίς ἤκουσεν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ φωνῆς εἰσποιούσης σε υἱὸν τῷ θεῷ; πλὴν ὅτι σὺ φῂς καί τινα ἕνα ἐπάγῃ τῶν μετὰ σοῦ κεκολασμένων.
pass_a_gloss: But so that we may not seem willingly (ἑκόντες), through being at a loss (ἀπορεῖν) for a reply (ἀπάντησις), to pass over (ὑπερβαίνειν) his headings (κεφάλαια), we decided (ἐκρίναμεν) to resolve (λῦσαι) according to [our] power each of the things put forward (προτιθεμένων) by him, taking thought (φροντίσαντες) not for the connection (εἱρμός) and sequence (ἀκολουθία) in the nature of the matters but for the order (τάξις) of what is written in his book. Come then, let us see what he says slandering (διαβάλλων) the Holy Spirit (πνεῦμα ἅγιον) seen (ἑωραμένον) as if bodily (οἷον σωματικῶς) by the Saviour in the form (εἴδει) of a dove; and it is the Jew (Ἰουδαῖος) with him still saying these things, to the one whom we confess (ὁμολογοῦμεν) to be our Lord (κύριον), Jesus: To you bathing (λουομένῳ), he says, beside John, you say an apparition (φάσμα) of a bird flew down out of the air. Then inquiring the Jew in his [book] says: what trustworthy witness saw this apparition, or who heard a voice from heaven adopting you as son to God? Except that you say [so] and bring in some one of those punished with you.
pass_b_english: But so that we may not seem to pass over his main points on purpose, for lack of an answer, we have decided to answer, as well as we can, each of the things he puts forward, paying attention not to the natural connection and sequence of the subjects but to the order of what is written in his book. Come, then, let us see what he says in slandering the Holy Spirit, seen by the Saviour, as it were bodily, in the form of a dove (Luke 3:22). It is still his Jew who says these things, speaking to the one whom we confess to be our Lord, Jesus: “When you were bathing beside John,” he says, “you say that an apparition of a bird flew down on you out of the air.” Then the Jew he has brought in goes on to ask: “What credible witness saw this apparition, or who heard a voice from heaven adopting you as God's Son (Matthew 3:17)? Except that you say so, and bring in one of those who were punished along with you.”

choices.choice: οἷον σωματικῶς ... εἴδει περιστερᾶς echoes Luke 3:22 (σωματικῷ εἴδει ὡς περιστεράν), hence the inline citation there. The Jew's words are Celsus's prosopopoeia; quotation marks follow the edition's sense division. εἰσποιούσης σε υἱὸν τῷ θεῷ: εἰσποιέω is the technical verb for adoption ('making you a son to God by adoption'); rendered 'adopting you as God's Son'. The voice is that of Matthew 3:17 (parallels Mark 1:11; Luke 3:22), cited inline as Matthew 3:17 only. 'One of those who were punished along with you' is left as the Greek has it; Origen in 1.43 takes it as a witness Christians bring in, and does not name him (John the Baptist, executed, is a possible referent, but this is uncertain).
'as though in bodily form, in the form of a dove' recast as 'as it were bodily, in the form of a dove' (οἷον σωματικῶς)
φάσμα ὄρνιθος: 'an apparition' (no article in the Greek)
voice citation narrowed to Matthew 3:17 (3:16 is the dove, not the voice); bible_refs updated
8 Greek lemma tags were moved from the gloss text into lemmas[] so the gloss reads as English; no gloss words changed.
